sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Hill (1942) retains the combination Eutermes fumigatus Brauer, 1865, with the type locality Sydney. The alate is small, its colour varying from pale brown to medium dark brown, with the head, thorax and abdomen hairy and the fontanelle large and distinct; the soldier is small with a pale head; there is usually a fairly distinct hyaline area between the media and the cubitus at the base of the wing.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Small, the colour varying from pale brown to medium dark brown, the postclypeus orange yellow to pale brown, the wings brown, usually with a fairly distinct hyaline area between the media and the cubitus at the base of the wing. Head, thorax and abdomen hairy. Fontanelle large, very distinct, elongate, narrowing behind and widening in front. Postclypeus slightly less than half as long as wide. Compound eyes variable in size, fairly prominent. Ocelli broadly oval, far from the compound eyes (Fig. 114). Teeth 1 and 2 of the left mandible equal in size. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 the smallest; segments 4 and 6 larger than segment 5. Pronotum small, distinctly narrower than the head, the anterior margin nearly straight, the anterior angles not contracted, the sides broadly rounded, contracting very little towards the posterior margin, the posterior margin slightly wavy to deeply concave; the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum variable but usually broadly and rather deeply concave. Cubitus with 12—15 branches. Measurements: length with wings 10.00—12.00; length without wings 5.00—6.00; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.06—1.14; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.66—0.73; head width 1.05—1.10; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.29—0.36; ocellus length 0.07—0.10; pronotum length 0.48—0.55; pronotum width 0.74—0.80; fore wing length 8.50—9.50; fore wing width 2.40—2.66.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Small, with a pale head. Head pale orange yellow, sometimes tinged with pale brown, rostrum pale rusty, antennae a deeper orange yellow, maxillary palpi and abdominal tergites paler than the antennae, legs straw-coloured. Head with very few hairs, the rostrum long, variable in basal width but always rather broad, about two-fifths of the length of the head capsule, the sides of the head nearly straight, the head (excluding the rostrum) broadly oval in dorsal view (Figs. 115, 116). Antennae usually 13-segmented, rarely 12; with 13 segments, segments 2, 3 and 5 about equal in length, segment 4 the shortest, segments 6—12 slightly longer than segment 5, segment 13 about as long as segment 5; with 12 segments, segment 3 usually the shortest. Mandibles usually pointed. Measurements: total length 3.25—3.75; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.28—1.50; head width 0.75—0.88; pronotum width 0.40—0.44. Abnormal individuals commonly occur together with normal ones, with a short, strongly curved rostrum and as few as 9 antennal segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head tinged with pale red hairs, orange yellow, tinged with pale brown in the posterior half, the postclypeus and antennae pale yellow. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 4 the shortest. Postclypeus slightly more than half as long as wide. Measurements: total length 3.25—3.50; head length (to anterior margin of clypeus) 1.21; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.69; head width 0.99; pronotum width 0.58.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen: total length 17.50; abdominal width 4.50 (the original OCR reads "17-50" and "4-50", with the decimal points recognised as hyphens).

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original uses the old combination Eutermes fumigatus (now placed in Nasutitermes). The synonymy list (several references from 1865—1932) is not translated entry by entry. The queen measurements are printed in the original as "17-50" and "4-50" and are transcribed as 17.50 and 4.50 with a note.
